root_cause.text: Newly allocated folios in ntfs_get_frame_pages() are not zero-initialized, so when the caller expects to completely overwrite the frame and skips reading from disk (ni_read_frame()), the folio contains uninitialized memory that can later be read by compression routines like longest_match_std(), causing information leakage or undefined behavior.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `__GFP_ZERO` to the `gfp_mask` passed to `__filemap_get_folio()` with `FGP_CREAT`. The commit message explicitly states: "When new folios are allocated without being marked uptodate and ni_read_frame() is skipped because the caller expects the frame to be completely overwritten, some reserved folios may remain only partially filled, leaving the rest memory uninitialized."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add __GFP_ZERO to guarantee zero-initialized folios in ntfs_get_frame_pages, avoiding potential information leaks or corruption from uninitialized data.
intent_record.what: Added __GFP_ZERO flag to gfp_mask when calling __filemap_get_folio, ensuring any newly allocated folio is zero-initialized.
intent_record.how: New folios created by __filemap_get_folio will now be zeroed before use, preventing exposure of uninitialized kernel memory in NTFS frame pages.
